title: President Donald Trump declines to name a successor but says Secretary of State Marco Rubio would be a ‘great’ option to lead the Republican Party: ‘Maybe I’m better off not getting involved’
content:
President Donald Trump has declined to commit to endorsing a successor in the 2028 presidential race, but singled out Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a “great” potential candidate. In his first sit-down interview since Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, Trump told CBS’s 60 Minutes that he might be better off staying out of the contest altogether. Notably, Trump’s refusal to endorse a candidate for 2028 at this stage came after several of his endorsed candidates in the 2026 midterms won the primaries but ultimately lost the general elections.

Donald Trump leaves 2028 endorsement decision open

Asked by 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat whether he would endorse a candidate in 2028, Trump replied, “Probably, not necessarily.” When asked what factors would influence his decision to endorse someone, he said, “I don’t know, we have a tremendous bench. I mean, I have so many people that I have great relationships with.” When pressed to name potential successors beyond the vice president, Trump mentioned Rubio. “Well, I think Marco’s great,” he said. However, he suggested the secretary of state would probably remain in his current position. “I think so. I mean, he certainly loves it, and he’s doing great. He’s doing a fantastic job,” Trump said.

Trump declined to identify other contenders. “There are many others. And I’d rather not mention their names,” he said, adding that some senators would also make excellent candidates.

He concluded, “Maybe I’m better off not getting involved.”

J.D. Vance’s position remains uncertain

Trump did not mention Vice President J.D. Vance by name during the conversation with Douthat. Vance entered the discussion only when Douthat asked about potential successors, leaving Trump without explicitly endorsing him. The omission came four days after Vance attributed the Republicans’ midterm losses to the war with Iran.

“The reason we lost is the war,” he wrote on X the morning after the election. “The president himself said so last night.”

Pre-midterm polls place J.D. Vance ahead in Republican field

Polling conducted before the midterms offers an indication of the current Republican field. The RealClearPolling average of national Republican primary surveys puts Vance at 38%, followed by Rubio at 26% and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis at 8%. Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, who might be among the senators Trump referred to in his conversation with Douthat, stands at approximately 3%.

Prediction markets see post-election shifts

Notably, prediction markets have registered changes since the midterms. As of Sunday, November 8, Polymarket gave Vance a 32% chance of securing the nomination, followed by Rubio at 21% and DeSantis at approximately 15%. Vance had been at 56% when the market launched in July 2025.

Kalshi showed a similar order, with Vance at 34%, Rubio at 21% and DeSantis at 17%. DeSantis recorded the week’s biggest movement on the platform, gaining approximately 13 percentage points as Vance declined.

Kalshi traders also assigned Rubio a 55% chance of leaving the administration this year, contrasting with Trump’s expectation that the secretary of state will remain in his position.

title: ‘They will subpoena me for sure’: Former Border Patrol boss Greg Bovino says he expects Democrats to target him once they take control of Congress in January
content:
Former U.S. Border Patrol Commander-at-Large Greg Bovino expects Democrats to subpoena him when they assume control of Congress in January, following their sweeping win in the midterm elections. In a statement to reporters, the Border Patrol veteran with nearly 30 years of experience said he anticipated congressional scrutiny after being pushed out of the Trump administration amid a series of fatal shootings involving immigration officers.

Greg Bovino expects congressional subpoena when Dems take office

“I think they will subpoena me for sure,” Bovino told Newsweek, anticipating that Democrats will seek his testimony once the new Congress convenes in January. Bovino became one of the most prominent figures in President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown efforts, overseeing high-profile enforcement operations in Los Angeles, Chicago and Minneapolis. During nearly three decades with the Border Patrol, he led the El Centro Sector and served in the agency’s tactical unit, BORTAC, before moving into senior leadership positions.

Reports say Bovino’s enforcement methods also attracted legal challenges. In Chicago, U.S. District Judge Sara Ellis ordered him to testify in litigation concerning immigration agents’ use of force. Following his deposition, Ellis described him as having appeared “evasive.”

Controversies surrounding Greg Bovino’s remarks

According to reports, Bovino also faced scrutiny over controversial remarks he allegedly made during a January 12 conference call involving federal officials in Minnesota. Citing multiple sources familiar with the discussion, CBS News reported that he expressed frustration after learning that U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen, an Orthodox Jew, could not attend a Saturday meeting because of the Sabbath. One source quoted Bovino as asking, “Do Orthodox criminals also take off on Saturday?” He also allegedly used the phrase “chosen people” disparagingly.

Democrats sought investigations into fatal shootings involving immigration officers

Bovino’s anticipated congressional questioning came after Democrats repeatedly demanded investigations into shootings involving federal immigration officers. In July, committee Democrats sought an investigation after an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston. Their letter requested body-camera and vehicle-camera footage, communications about the operation, information concerning the officer and records supporting DHS’ public account. House Democrats also demanded independent investigations into the deaths of Ruben Ray Martinez, a U.S. citizen fatally shot by an ICE agent in Texas in March 2025, and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, who was killed during an ICE operation in Maine in July 2026.

Democratic takeover of Congress could intensify DHS scrutiny

The midterm results gave Democrats control of both the House and Senate, significantly expanding their ability to investigate the Trump administration when the new Congress takes office in January. Control of House committees will give Democrats access to investigative powers, including the ability to issue subpoenas. Their Senate majority will also create additional opportunities to closely examine DHS operations and immigration enforcement policies.

title: ‘Ultimately, that hurt me’: President Donald Trump says his mass deportation policies were ‘too tough’
content:
President Donald Trump has acknowledged that his mass deportation policies may have been “too tough,” saying they ultimately hurt him politically in the midterm elections. In an interview with CBS’ 60 Minutes, Trump said his administration had succeeded in securing the southern border but acknowledged that deporting immigrants without criminal records who worked and paid taxes had alienated some voters. The president also suggested he could negotiate with Democrats over legal protections for certain undocumented immigrants.

Donald Trump admits deportation policy might have gone too far: ‘I think it was too tough’

Speaking with 60 Minutes host Ross Douthat on Sunday, November 8, Trump said he believed his effort to secure the southern border deserved “an A+,” but acknowledged that his aggressive deportation campaign had affected the midterm election results. “I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out, but I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation for breaking the law: they came into the country illegally,” Trump said.

When asked whether he believed his deportation policy had gone too far, the president replied, “I think it was too tough,” Trump said. “I think it might be too tough, yeh. A lot of people would say that it’s great, but a lot of people think it’s too tough. I think, ultimately, that hurt me.”

It is worth noting that immigration ranked below the cost of living and the state of democracy among voters’ midterm concerns, marking a shift from 2024, when border security and illegal immigration were prominent election issues.

Donald Trump defends his border record

Trump defended his efforts to reduce illegal border crossings, claiming that 25 million people had entered the country during former President Joe Biden’s four years in office. “We had 25 million people come in through Biden over a four-year period, and many of those people were, as you know, they were from prisons, they were drug dealers, they were from mental institutions, they were from all over the world, not just South America,” Trump said. U.S. Customs and Border Protection has said there have been no releases into the country’s interior of people who crossed the border illegally over the past 17 months. Under Biden, asylum seekers were commonly released while their cases were pending.

However, Trump acknowledged the consequences of deporting people working in hotels and landscaping businesses and earning an honest living, including those who paid taxes. Describing a hotel worker detained by ICE, he said, “It’s tough. It’s a tough thing.”

Donald Trump floats possible deal with Democrats on immigration

Trump suggested that undocumented immigrants without criminal records could receive some form of legal status, saying an agreement with Democrats was achievable. “The deal would be, we would work something out, and I think that’s something that’s actually doable,” he said. Trump also said he could avoid insulting Democrats for six months if doing so helped secure an agreement. “Very easily,” he told Douthat.

The suggestion of making a deal with Democrats drew mixed reactions. While some Democrats as well as some Republicans welcomed the possibility, Trump’s MAGA supporters opposed any form of amnesty. Former senior Department of Homeland Security official Adam Klein cautioned that acknowledging the distinction between undocumented immigrants and criminal threats did not necessarily mean the administration would change its policies. “His suggestion that he could work with Democrats to allow some longtime residents to remain is interesting, but I would be careful about calling it a pathway to legal status,” Klein told Newsweek. “There is a difference between deciding not to deport someone and granting lawful status, and an even greater difference between temporary protection, permanent residence and citizenship.”

Bipartisan response to Donald Trump’s apparent shift in position

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer questioned Trump’s apparent change of direction, pointing to Stephen Miller’s appointment as White House chief of staff. “Trump says his immigration crackdown went too far. Apparently, his solution was to put the man responsible for it in charge of the White House,” Schumer posted on X. “That’s not a course correction. That’s a promotion.”

Republican Representative Maria Salazar of Florida urged Trump to pursue bipartisan immigration reform, arguing that immigration involved economic concerns beyond border security. She further said he could surpass Ronald Reagan’s legacy by delivering a historic reform. Notably, immigration laws have largely remained unchanged since the early 1990s, despite repeated bipartisan efforts to reform the system. New Jersey Democratic Representative Rob Menendez, meanwhile, called for an end to federal agents’ enforcement tactics. “The American people have spoken,” Menendez wrote. “Now the question is whether the President and his congressional enablers will do right by the country. Our communities deserve real, meaningful action, and that is what I and House Democrats are ready to deliver.”

Klein warned that a more moderate presidential statement did not guarantee a policy shift, particularly as Miller and others in the administration continued advocating tougher restrictions, including on legal immigration. “But I would not confuse an opening with a commitment,” Klein said. “We don’t yet know what Trump is willing to do, what Democrats can deliver, or whether either side can agree on something that meaningfully addresses the needs of immigrants, families, employers and the country.”

title: Former Donald Trump campaign staffer calls on the president to throw in the towel: ‘The country would be best off if he resigned and instead spent time enjoying his grandchildren’
content:
Donald Trump‘s former campaign staffer Matt Braynard has urged the president to step down following the Republican Party’s losses in the midterm elections.

In a post on X, Braynard praised Trump’s record but argued that his resignation could be rather beneficial.

“I believe President Trump is the best president of my lifetime in terms of getting things done that matter,” Braynard wrote before calling for Trump to leave office.

“I think that after tonight’s results, that he, the party, and the country would be best off if he resigned and instead spent time enjoying his grandchildren,” he added.

Who is Matt Braynard?

Braynard is an experienced political strategist who has been actively involved in U.S. politics for several years. He has worked on five presidential campaigns, including Trump’s first bid for the White House.

He also founded Look Ahead America, a nonprofit organization focused on encouraging voter participation/

Matt Braynard’s role in Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign and Look Ahead America

Braynard previously served as director of technology for Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign. However, the campaign dismissed him in April 2016, months before the general election. At the time, it was reported that his departure created problems with access to campaign data, with the operation reportedly struggling to retrieve some of its own information.

Braynard later founded Look Ahead America, a conservative organization established in 2017. The group became known for supporting individuals prosecuted over their involvement in the January 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol and organizing rallies on their behalf.

Look Ahead America also filed a lawsuit against the Stark County Board of Elections in Ohio in 2021. The complaint challenged closed-door discussions concerning the possible purchase of Dominion Voting Systems equipment. In 2024, the Supreme Court of Ohio ordered a new trial in the case.

Matt Braynard links to pro-Donald Trump online campaigns

Braynard also gained attention for his involvement in online political activism during the 2016 election cycle. He was described as one of the figures behind the so-called “Great Meme War,” a decentralized online campaign that circulated pro-Trump and anti-Hillary Clinton material.

Participants in the online movement claimed their efforts helped Trump win the election. Braynard later became involved in other Republican political initiatives, including efforts to encourage Virginia Republicans to increase mail-in voting in 2024.

His background in campaign technology and conservative advocacy has kept him connected to the broader Republican movement.

Matt Braynard signals support for J.D. Vance’s independent political role

In a separate post on X, Braynard defended J.D. Vance’s position within the Trump administration and emphasized that the vice president holds an independent constitutional role.

“An important fact: [Vance] is not an employee of the President and does not serve at anyone’s pleasure,” Braynard wrote. “He was elected by the people and has his own constitutional authority and agency, and he can chart whatever course he believes is best for the future of the country.”

His remarks prompted disagreement from one social media user, who argued that voters had elected Trump rather than Vance and had not directly chosen the vice president. Braynard responded, “You should have looked more closely at the names on your ballot.”

title: Former President Joe Biden says ‘some days are better than others’ as he battles stage four cancer: ‘It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down’
content:
Former President Joe Biden has acknowledged that his battle with stage four prostate cancer continues to affect his daily life, admitting that “some days are better than others.”

In a recent post on X, Biden said treatment had not stopped him but sometimes slowed him down, explaining that his health would limit promotional appearances for his upcoming presidential memoir, Promise Me, America. The update came more than a year after his May 2025 diagnosis and follows months of therapy, treatment and occasional health updates from his family.

Joe Biden acknowledges cancer’s impact on his daily life

Biden’s post on Sunday, November 8, focused largely on his presidential memoir, scheduled for release on November 17. He said the book covers “the challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them.” However, he acknowledged that his health would prevent him from undertaking all the planned promotional appearances. “Some days are better than others,” Biden wrote. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down.”

“Unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves,” he added.

The memoir will also address his decision to seek reelection before stepping aside, a subject that has drawn criticism from both parties over questions about how truthful his team was about his health while he was president. Biden’s team has denied any cover-up.

Joe Biden diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer in May 2025

Biden’s cancer was discovered approximately four months after he left the White House. In May 2025, worsening urinary symptoms prompted medical examinations that revealed a prostate nodule. He was diagnosed on May 16, and his office announced the diagnosis on Sunday, May 18.

The cancer had spread to his bones and was classified as Gleason score 9, Grade Group 5, placing it among the most aggressive forms of prostate cancer. His office nevertheless offered some reassurance, saying “the cancer appears to be hormone-sensitive which allows for effective management.” At the time, Biden wrote on Facebook, “Like so many of you, [my wife] Jill and I have learned that we are strongest in the broken places.”

Joe Biden underwent radiation and hormone treatment throughout 2025

Biden subsequently underwent treatment throughout 2025. In September, spokesperson Kelly Scully confirmed he had undergone Mohs surgery to remove skin cancer after a healing wound appeared on his forehead. On October 11, Scully said Biden was “currently undergoing radiation therapy and hormone treatment.” Nine days later, on October 20, she confirmed that he had completed radiation therapy at Penn Medicine Radiation Oncology in Philadelphia. It was reported at the time that Biden also “rang the bell” at the facility, marking the end of his radiation course. However, the milestone did not mean the cancer had disappeared, and Scully did not disclose what treatment would follow.

Biden family offered periodic updates about former president’s health

In August, Jill Biden told SiriusXM’s “Let’s Talk Off Camera with Kelly Ripa” that her husband was “doing okay” but added that “he will forever live with cancer, and we have to be mindful of it every three months, testing and medicines.” Days later, Hunter Biden told the BBC’s Newsnight that the cancer had spread further, describing it as “very painful and very debilitating in many respects.” In September, however, the president said on X that “the radiation treatment from last fall worked as intended.”

His latest health update contrasts with his July 15 announcement, when he described treatment as “going really well” and promoted plans for a book tour and interviews. He concluded Sunday’s post by recalling his father’s advice. “Looking forward, I’m going to keep following what my father told me a long time ago: ‘Champ, when you get knocked down, get up,’” he wrote. “It’s a good lesson for me. And for America.”

title: Jon Stewart takes aim at Democrats, urges the party to avoid thinking they ‘get to impeach everybody’ now that they control Congress, says Chuck Schumer ‘does not understand the urgency of the moment’
content:
Jon Stewart has urged Democrats to prioritize rebuilding their party’s leadership and addressing voters’ concerns rather than treating their newly secured congressional majorities as an opportunity to pursue impeachment proceedings. Following the party’s recent electoral victories, the comedian argued that Democrats must use their political advantage to govern effectively instead of focusing primarily on confronting President Donald Trump.

On a recent episode of “The Weekly Show,” Stewart also criticized Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer. He argued that Democrats should reconsider their reliance on seniority when selecting congressional leaders and make room for representatives who can better connect with voters.

Jon Stewart says Democrats should focus on governing, not impeachment

Stewart addressed the party’s next steps during a question-and-answer segment at the end of his podcast. One viewer jokingly asked whether actor George Clooney should write an opinion piece urging Schumer to step down. Clooney previously attracted attention during the 2024 presidential campaign when he publicly encouraged then-President Joe Biden to reconsider his reelection bid.

Responding to the question, Stewart said Democrats should treat their latest victories as an opportunity to challenge the political practices that contributed to their earlier difficulties.

“By the way, that’s job one of this opportunity. Job one of this opportunity is to tear down the obstacles and old way of thinking that got us into this mess. Someone has to meet this moment and they have got to show — and this moment is not, ‘Oh, we get to impeach everybody,’ like f*** that. Like, you have an opportunity to actually govern. Do it. Take it,” he said.

Jon Stewart criticizes Chuck Schumer and Democratic leadership

The comedian also questioned Schumer’s influence within the party, arguing that seniority should not automatically determine who occupies its most powerful congressional positions.

He criticized Democrats who credited Schumer for helping secure the party’s recent victories, claiming the senator had previously opposed several of the candidates who contributed to those results.

“And one of the first things you need to do is remove that system of seniority from Democratic politics. It is a b******* system and it needs to go,” he said.

Stewart added that Schumer “does not understand the urgency of the moment and what the future demands,” emphasizing that he genuinely believes the party needs a different approach.

His criticism also raises questions about House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries’ position. Neither Schumer nor Jeffries automatically retains their leadership role because of their current standing.

AIPAC’s support for Democratic candidates draws progressive criticism

Stewart’s remarks ca\ome amid wider disagreements within the Democratic Party over its leadership, political priorities and relationship with pro-Israel advocacy groups.

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) congratulated Schumer and Jeffries following the election victories. In a statement, the organization said more than 234 candidates supported by its members had won their races, while several contests remained undecided.

However, progressive Democrats have criticized both leaders over their relationship with AIPAC and what they view as insufficient support for candidates such as New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

title: Tech giant Nvidia opens investigation after CEO Jensen Huang tells staff he had an affair with a woman allegedly identified as a Chinese spy by US officials
content:
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he acknowledged having an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence agencies identified as an alleged Beijing spy. The disclosure follows reports that the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to gather information about the billionaire executive and potentially influence the chipmaker’s business with China. Nvidia’s board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and Jensen will remain CEO while the investigation proceeds.

Nvidia launches independent investigation into CEO

Nvidia announced the investigation on Sunday, November 8, after Jensen, the company’s co-founder, informed its board about his relationship with Alice. The independent directors will select outside counsel to examine the available information, with company spokesman John Rizzo confirming that Jensen will have no role in choosing the investigator. The board said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.” It added that Jensen “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.”

According to reports, Jensen apologized for the affair in a message to employees, acknowledging the personal consequences of the relationship. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

U.S. intelligence suspects Alice Huang was a spy

The relationship became a national security concern after U.S. agencies began electronic surveillance of Alice more than a year ago. According to intelligence cited in reports, officials concluded she was communicating information directly to Beijing and had been recruited to target the Nvidia CEO.

It has been further reported that a highly classified memo circulated among senior U.S. officials this past spring described her as an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Intelligence officials reportedly believed she could gather information about Jensen and potentially influence Nvidia to support making its most advanced chips available to China.

According to reports, Alice was a senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that rents Nvidia computing power to Alibaba and other Chinese businesses. U.S. officials suspect Megaspeed helped smuggle restricted artificial intelligence chips into China, although the Chinese embassy has dismissed the allegations as “smears.”

Megaspeed dealings and relationship draw scrutiny

Megaspeed, formed in 2023, became a major Nvidia customer in Southeast Asia, purchasing more than $4.8 billion in chips since June 2024. Nvidia continued doing business with the company despite a Commerce Department investigation into suspected chip-smuggling activities. Both Jensen and Nvidia initially described his dealings with Alice as ordinary business interactions. In an interview with Bloomberg News last month, he said their interactions were “related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual.”

However, surveillance reportedly established that their relationship was romantic. Their interactions included meetings in Taipei in June 2024 and a restaurant dinner the following year, where Taiwanese media photographed Alice kissing Jensen on the cheek.

Donald Trump defends Nvidia CEO as investigation begins

President Donald Trump defended Jensen on Sunday, saying he had not heard that the executive had done anything wrong. “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it,” Trump said, adding that Jensen had done “an amazing job for our country.”

Asked whether he should remain CEO, Trump replied, “I think so. Oh, yes, sure.”

Trump also said he would “certainly take him” on his upcoming China trip, despite acknowledging that he had not discussed the matter with Jensen. 

Meanwhile, Sen. Elizabeth Warren said Jensen and Nvidia’s board “owe Congress answers” about his relationship with the alleged spy.

Rep. Michael McCaul, a Texas Republican, called for an immediate pause in advanced AI chip shipments to China until the allegations are investigated.

Nvidia, meanwhile, insisted that the inquiry will not interrupt Jensen’s leadership. “Today’s news will not slow Nvidia,” Rizzo said.

title: President Donald Trump insists he was ‘only kidding’ about Dana White joining his administration as White House press secretary, says UFC CEO ‘loves the idea’
content:
President Donald Trump has clarified that his announcement offering Dana White the position of White House Press Secretary was a joke, although he says the UFC CEO “loves the idea.” Trump made the comments to reporters in Palm Beach, Florida, on Sunday, November 8, a day after publicly inviting White to take the job on Truth Social.

Donald Trump says White House job offer to Dana White was a joke

Trump addressed the announcement Sunday, insisting that his Saturday post was not a serious appointment offer. “You would have thought that people would have said, ‘He’s having a good time!’” Trump said. “I will tell you, I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea!” Later Sunday night, he reiterated, “I was kidding, of course,” while confirming that White still intended to visit him on Monday.

The president had initially announced the supposed offer to White on Truth Social, describing him as “a violent Fighter and Warrior.”

“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” Trump wrote. “Dana, please take the job!”

Donald Trump proposes MMA figures as Dana White’s assistants

Trump’s post also suggested that White bring several prominent mixed martial arts personalities into the administration as assistants. The names included Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harris. The president said the group would be needed to “defend us against the Lunatic Left.”

White responded shortly after the announcement while attending an event in London. He said he planned to fly to Washington, D.C., to meet Trump on Monday and shared an AI-generated image of himself standing behind the White House press secretary podium. Trump also shared an animated video briefly showing how White’s tenure as White House press secretary would go. The video showed anyone disagreeing with or criticizing Trump facing the wrath of several iconic MMA fighters.

White House press secretary position remains vacant

The White House press secretary position has been unfilled since Katie Zacharia’s brief tenure ended on October 9. Announced as the new press secretary in early October, Zacharia began the job on October 5 but left after just five days.

Before her appointment, Karoline Leavitt served as Trump’s press secretary for the first 584 days of his second term. A spokesperson for his 2024 presidential campaign before joining the administration, Leavitt returned to the White House following her maternity leave for several months before announcing her departure in the summer.

Dana White’s Washington visit still expected

Although Trump dismissed the announcement as a joke, White is still expected to meet the president on Monday, although the agenda of their meeting is still unknown. For now, Trump has yet to announce a replacement for Zacharia, and the White House press secretary position remains vacant.

title: President Donald Trump says Israel and ‘the entire Middle East’ would not ‘exist today’ if he hadn’t shut down Iran’s nuclear program: ‘Nobody wants to say that, but everybody knows it’s true’
content:
After the Republican Party’s historic midterm defeat, President Donald Trump took the credit for saving Israel and the “entire” Middle East.

On November 7, Trump shared a post on Truth Social claiming that his intervention prevented Iran from developing nuclear weapons and asserting that both Israel and the Middle East would otherwise no longer exist.

“Israel and, in fact, the entire Middle East, WOULD NOT EXIST TODAY if I did not stop Iran from having a Nuclear Weapon. Nobody wants to say that, but everybody knows it’s true!” he wrote.

Pressure at home

The comments came after the GOP faced a drastic midterm defeat, with Democrats winning control of the House and Senate.

Particularly alarming for the GOP was data from the midterm defeat that showed voters under 30 shifted towards Democrats, reversing gains made by Trump in the 2024 presidential election.

Unfortunately for the GOP, the data also showed that Hispanic, Latino and Black voters followed young voters to the left. 

Donald Trump has no regrets about the Iran war

While many, including Vice President J.D. Vance, do not approve of the war with Iran, Trump asserted that he had to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. However, Trump did not disagree with Vance, admitting that the war is one of the reasons the GOP lost the midterm elections.

“Well, I think it’s largely true, because it drove gasoline up a little bit short-term. And probably that’s — that’s probably it’s true. But at the same time, if I had to do it again, I’d have to do it again, because long-term, it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon,” Trump said.

When asked if the war with Iran is worth it, he replied, “I do [think so], yeah. Well, we have no choice. I thought oil would go up a lot more. You have no choice. You have to do it. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon — or everything that you see here some day might not exist.”

Unresolved conflict

After almost eight months of U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran and Tehran’s retaliation against Gulf countries with U.S. military bases, the conflict has created plenty of diplomatic and military challenges for Washington.

In a conversation with reporters in the Oval Office on November 7, Trump said he would decide whether to resume military operations and that the objective of strikes is to ensure that Iran’s nuclear program is permanently dismantled.

“I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You’ll know soon enough,” Trump said.

Iran‘s conditions

According to a November 5 Reuters report, Iran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar. The proposal included lifting U.S. sanctions, releasing frozen Iranian assets, receiving compensation for war damages, ending the U.S. naval blockade and downsizing the military presence in the region.

Washington is now in a tight spot, with Tehran refusing to negotiate or reopen the Strait of Hormuz until all demands are met.

title: Boston Blue's [Spoiler] Recalls Past Suicide Attempt in Emotional Reveal
content:
Boston Blue‘s newest episode took an emotional turn when a main character revealed a past suicide attempt.

During the Friday, November 13, episode of the CBS series, Sean Reagan (Mika Amonsen) and Jonah Silver (Marcus Scribner) searched for a fellow officer, whom they believed was a risk to himself. They were able to talk him down after Sean revealed his own mental health challenges. He specifically recalled struggling with suicidal ideation after his mother’s death and how a past attempt had pushed him to address his issues.

Before Boston Blue, Sean’s journey was featured on Blue Bloods, which ran from 2010 to 2024. The spinoff, which premiered in October 2025, kicked off with Danny (Donnie Wahlberg) visiting Boston after Sean ended up in a coma. This version of Sean looked a little different, as Andrew Terraciano previously played the role.

“There’s been some negativity [from viewers], for sure,” Amonsen exclusively told Us in November 2025 about taking over the part. “But when I look under those posts that have the negativity, there’s a lot of fans rallying for Sean and people saying that they really enjoyed this character that I’ve created — or my version of character.”

Mika Amonsen Breaks Silence on 'Boston Blue' Recasting Andrew Terraciano

Amonsen noted that he wanted to make Blue Bloods fans happy with his performance, saying, “They’re really enjoying the show, and they love where it’s going in terms of Sean, and that makes me happy.”

The actor recalled feeling “a ton of pressure” over the situation.

“I felt the pressure to respect an actor before me because I wanted to respect Andrew the best I could. There were even certain visual choices that I made that I wanted to keep in terms of hair styling and certain ways of being [as Sean],” he continued. “I really want to maintain Sean as close as I can in the ways that I do it out of respect for this character that everyone loves — but also the character Andrew built.”

He continued: “When I booked the show, it all happened really quickly. It was within about a week’s time, and I was really thrown into it quickly. I did binge-watch as much as I could, and I found doing the later seasons was more helpful. I wanted to get a sense of who Sean was toward the end of the show. I really wanted to get a sense of his character at that point into adulthood and his relationship with Danny.”

Blue Bloods' Andrew Terraciano Breaks Silence on the Spinoff Recasting Sean

Terraciano, meanwhile, broke his silence to Us about the shakeup.

“I had somebody call me — actually the day that I was graduating — and they had spoken to my mom, and she called me [crying]. They were like, ‘They might be looking for a different Sean,'” Terraciano shared with Us in December about the onscreen change. “Shortly after we got the news, Donnie called me. It was a really beautiful moment of getting to hear from an old friend but also somebody that you respect so much and have learned so much from.”

Terraciano expressed gratitude for his time on Blue Bloods.

“It’s beautiful because you’ll always remember every single line and every day that you had the opportunity to be that character,” he shared. “It doesn’t mean for even a second that somebody else can’t go and do something beautiful with it.”

Terraciano continued: “I got the joy of playing Sean, and I got to send him off into the world. Now somebody else gets that joy. We’re both getting to show what we do and then send Sean off into the world.”

Boston Blue airs on CBS Fridays at 10 p.m. ET.

title: Golden Bachelorette's Joan Vassos Reveals Why She and Chock Chapple Split
content:
Joan Vassos is sharing candid details about why she and Chock Chapple called off their engagement.

The Golden Bachelorette star, 63, reflected on the breakup in an interview with People on Friday, November 13, explaining why the couple ultimately weren’t meant to be.

Vasso told the outlet that she had hoped their relationship would lead to marriage but things didn’t quite work out as planned.

“When Chock got down on one knee, I was like, ‘I think I can do this. I’m ready to make this leap of faith. I actually have enough faith in this relationship to think that it might really succeed, that we might really get married,’” Vassos recalled.

Golden Bachelorette's Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple Split After 2 Years

The reality star added that she had also prepared herself for the possibility that their romance might not last, telling herself, “If it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out.”

Over the course of their two-year engagement, Vassos and Chapple, also 63, shared plenty of major milestones, from introducing each other to their families and taking vacations together to navigating some difficult moments.

“We did a lot,” Vassos told the outlet. “I had two sons get married, three grandbabies born. I mean, a lot happened in our two years of engagement. We did all the things.”

The pair also supported each other through Chapple’s recent medical challenges. In August, he revealed that he had undergone surgery to have his prostate removed following a cancer scare.

“When you go through something medically, that really tests a relationship, and I felt like we did so much of this really well,” Vassos said.

Ultimately, however, the former couple came to the realization that they weren’t the right match.

“We figured out that we weren’t each other’s person, and that’s okay,” she explained.

Despite the heartbreak, Vassos said the relationship taught her a great deal about herself and what she wants from a future partner.

“I grew immensely in that time,” she shared. “I figured out what I need from a relationship. I figured out that I can actually fall in love with somebody again.”

“It wasn’t like any part of this relationship was ever miserable. It’s just we weren’t each other’s people,” she continued. “I’m grateful for the whole thing, even though the ending wasn’t what I wanted.”

Vassos and Chapple announced their decision to end their engagement on November 6, sharing statements via their respective Instagram Stories.

Golden Bachelorette Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple’s Relationship Timeline

“Two years ago, Chock and I took a leap of faith and got engaged during our season of The Golden Bachelorette, hoping we had found our forever,” Vassos wrote at the time. “We spent the last two years living what we hoped would be the beginning of our love story, sharing our families, amazing adventures, laughter, and supporting each other through challenging times.”

“Sadly, our journey hasn’t turned out the way we had hoped and we have decided to end our engagement,” she continued. “We truly want each other to be happy, and I’m grateful for the chapter we shared.”

Chapple later shared a similarly worded statement of his own.

The couple first found love during the inaugural season of ABC’s The Golden Bachelorette in 2024, with Chapple proposing to Vassos during the season finale.

title: 'Life With Derek' Stepsiblings Leaned Into 'Undeniable Chemistry' Onscreen
content:
Life With Derek’s Michael Seater has always been well aware of fan chatter about the dynamic he shared with his onscreen stepsister.

During a recent appearance on the “Back to the Best” podcast, Seater, 39, confessed that he and costar, Ashley Leggat, 40, purposely leaned in to their “undeniable chemistry” despite playing family members.

“Here’s the thing, we had an undeniable chemistry that fans loved,” Seater noted.

Life With Derek was a Canadian TV show broadcast via Disney Channel in the United States from 2005 to 2009. Leggat starred as Casey McDonald while Seater played the role of Derek Venturi. In the show, Casey’s mom married Derek’s dad, making them stepsiblings. However, viewers were convinced there was an underlying sexual tension between the two.

Does Robbie Amell Think 'Life With Derek' Was About Stepsiblings in Love?

“Listen, romance has never been bigger, right?” Seater said, before joking that fans seemingly would have loved Derek and Casey to follow some sort of enemies-to-lovers trope.

“So fans want that and they’re like, well they’re stepsiblings so technically…” he quipped.

Seater said he and Leggat knew how fans perceived their dynamic at the time that the show was being made.

“In these early days of the internet, our producers don’t know that there’s like forums online where people are talking, but we do,” Seater recalled. “We saw that the fans were talking about it. And so, and I can say this because I’ve said it a million times, we knew that the fans liked it, so we leaned into it without letting the writers or the producers know that we were leaning into it.”

Seater recounted how there were times on set during production that the show’s crew had to make changes so the characters didn’t appear to be getting too close for comfort.

“One of those showrunners would be like, ‘No, we can’t use that… Don’t use those shots. Like, it’s too much,’” Seater laughed. “And we’d be, like, sitting on a couch and they’d be like, ‘Can you maybe separate yourselves a little on the couch?’”

Celebrities Who Secretly Dated Their Costars Behind the Scenes

Jokes aside, Seater praised Leggat as a colleague, describing her as his “favorite scene partner.”

“I could always do anything, you felt so safe. In comedy you want to be able to try stuff and play around and it’s not always going to land,” he explained.

Seater continued, “We just always had each other’s back and we were always just going for it.”

The actor added that he felt like his and Legget’s rapport with one another was a crucial aspect in the show’s success.

“That’s the show and you know that is the engine of the show. It had to be that these two people had this amazing chemistry and could bounce off each other,” Seater said.

title: How Joey Graziadei's Fiancee Kelsey Reacted to Holiday Rom-Com Kissing Scene
content:
Joey Graziadei is officially a rom-com leading man, but there’s only one woman whose opinion matters to him: his fiancée Kelsey Anderson.

Graziadei, 31, revealed on the Thursday, November 12, episode of the “Viall Files” podcast that Anderson, 28, was “so funny” about his casting as single firefighter Dean in Roku Channel’s The Holiday Spark, especially when he told her there would be a movie makeout. (His character enlists Jamie Chung’s illustrator Laura to help plan a holiday party for his firehouse where a possible love connection ignites.)

“I got the offer and I asked first, ‘Does a holiday movie — is there a kiss?’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, there’s a kiss at the end,’” he recalled. “I’m like, ‘Alright, let me talk to Kelsey.’”

Joey Graziadei Admits to Struggles in Kelsey Relationship After 'Bachelor'

Anderson, however, was totally unfazed by the idea of him kissing another woman after the couple met on The Bachelor in 2023, getting engaged during the season 28 finale, which aired in 2024.

“Kelsey, like, literally laughed in my face,” Anderson remembered. “She’s like, ‘I saw you kiss all these girls on TV. This is literally the foundation of our relationship. If you think I’m going to keep you from getting your first acting opportunity, because there’s a kiss scene, you’re crazy.’”

Graziadei said he was just making sure she was cool with the idea, telling her, “I was like, ‘I’m trying to be a good fiancé.’ I’m asking.”

Graziadei noted that Anderson has always been supportive of his career, including his stint on Dancing With the Stars season 33.

Throughout the season, which he won, his connection with dance partner Jenna Johnson was criticized and questioned for being too cozy, but Anderson never took the bait and always backed Graziadei.

The Bachelor's Joey Graziadei Proposes to Kelsey Anderson Again

“If Kelsey for some reason said, ‘I just am not comfortable, I feel like it’s not something I want to keep dealing with.’ I wouldn’t be doing it,” Graziadei explained on the podcast. “That is my first and foremost, what I want in life is to make sure — this could all go away — I need to make sure that Kelsey and I are still good.”

He added that with everything that’s happened since they got engaged, he couldn’t be happier with his partner.

“The fact that she was so supportive of me, I’m just grateful,” Graziadei gushed.

Joey Graziadei Admits ‘DWTS’ Was ‘Difficult at Times’ on Kelsey Romance

Outside of The Holiday Spark, which is currently streaming on Roku, Graziadei has been focused on his and Anderson’s upcoming wedding.

“It’s fun man. We’re really close to the final stages of it all,” he shared of the planning process. “Welcome party’s locked. Venue’s locked. Location. Date. We’re finishing up our invites right now to get them out.”

The Traitors star added, “It’s been so much fun, because I’m like I can’t wait for the day to be here. But now, it’s also the point where it’s sneaking up a little bit.”

title: HBO’s 5-Part Crime Drama Has One of the Best Seasons in TV History

title: Woman Who Scammed Clayton Echard With Fake Pregnancy to Speak Out in New Doc
content:
A new documentary is expected to put the spotlight on Clayton Echard’s years-long legal battle with Laura Owens.

Peacock announced on Friday, November 13, that a four-part documentary titled Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens is set to premiere in 2027.

“Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens follows an astonishing story when Laura meets Clayton through a potential real estate deal and after their short connection, she tells him she’s pregnant with his twins,” the documentary’s logline states. “Their private dispute erupts into a nationally followed story fueled by citizen sleuths and social commentators that join the media firestorm that implodes into a shocking trail of deception, legal threats and public humiliation. The deeper the investigation goes, the more unbelievable the revelations become, while raising a disturbing question: when does the desire to be loved turn into an obsession?”

In a press release, Peacock confirmed the documentary will feature exclusive interviews with Echard, 33, his legal team and other men who were allegedly targeted by Owens, 36.

Everything Bachelor's Clayton Echard Has Said About His Paternity Lawsuit

For the first time, Owens will also share her experience and perspective in a new interview.

In August, Owens pleaded guilty to two counts of fraudulent schemes and artifices, one count of taking the identity of another and one count of perjury, Fox 10 Phoenix and Mercury News reported. Additional charges were dropped as part of her plea agreement.

“It’s the first time that we’ve seen Laura take any accountability in this matter,” Echard — who led season 26 of The Bachelor in 2022 — said via a TikTok video on August 29 before sharing his reaction to the plea. “I felt numb and emotionless. I couldn’t understand why that was.”

Every NFL Player Who's Been 'The Bachelor' Lead Through the Years

I’m grateful for this entire experience — I know that sounds backwards. The amount of resilience I’ve built through all of this, the community I have found with all of this adversity, the power of presence that I’ve gained. The insight. Everything that has come from all of this. I would do it 1,000 times over because I’m proud of the man I’ve become through it all.”

On October 23, Owens was sentenced to 30 days in jail and seven years of probation.

Owens and Echard’s legal battle was previously analyzed on iHeartRadio’s “Love Trapped” podcast. Hosted by Stephani Young, the podcast premiered in February, with the finale airing Thursday, November 12.

title: Who Was Matt Lambert? Doctor Identified as Shooter in D.C. Mass Shooting
content:
Authorities have identified the gunman behind a deadly mass shooting near a Washington, D.C., gym as Dr. Matt Lambert, a 55-year-old emergency medicine physician who was in the middle of an ongoing legal dispute with his condominium association.

Lambert shot five people in the city’s Logan Circle neighborhood on the morning of November 12, 2026, killing one person and injuring four others before dying by suicide. The gunfire began inside the VIDA gym and ended hours later inside a seventh-floor apartment in the building directly above the fitness club.

Matt Lambert Identified as Washington, D.C. Mass Shooter

Metropolitan Police Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll confirmed Lambert’s identity during a press conference, describing a gunman who began his rampage inside the gym before fleeing upstairs to barricade himself in a residential unit. Lambert was a licensed emergency medicine doctor who most recently worked as a healthcare consultant.

Oz Pearlman Details Moment He Locked Eyes With POTUS During WHCD Shooting

The person killed inside VIDA was James Stuart, the building manager. One of the surviving victims remains in critical condition after being shot in the head, while three others suffered non-life-threatening injuries.

Carroll said investigators quickly connected the violence to a civil matter Lambert had been pursuing against the people who managed his building. “We do know that the victim that was killed inside the VIDA was the building manager for that location. So, we do know that there has been an ongoing dispute between the suspect in this case and the building, condo, homeowners association, management regarding maintenance issues—mold and the like—that there was a civil case that he filed against them. So, we believe that it’s related to that,” Carroll said.

Inside Matt Lambert’s Condo Association Lawsuit

Lambert purchased the 1,200-square-foot penthouse inside the building for $1.095 million in 2016. Five years later, he listed the home for $1.275 million, according to online listings cited by NBC Washington.

Lambert filed his lawsuit against the condominium association in 2025, claiming he had started noticing mold, moisture and water problems inside the apartment in 2024 after a contractor worked on the building. He alleged the damage cost him more than $100,000 and sued for negligence, breach of fiduciary duty and nuisance. He also requested a jury trial.

The case was still active at the time of the shooting. A mediation session had been scheduled for March 2027.

Matt Lambert’s Attorney Speaks Out

Joel Braithwaite, Lambert’s attorney, said he was surprised by the violence and pushed back against any suggestion that the civil case had been a signal of what was to come.

“I don’t want the story to be that litigation led to this result. Litigation is supposed to prevent these results by having people litigate in court and not have that spill into the streets,” Braithwaite said.

Braithwaite said Lambert owned several residences but considered the D.C. penthouse his “prized possession.” He described a client who felt singled out by the people who ran the building.

“One of the issues for us was that Matt was treated differently than a lot of other people in the units, and that was the source of some consternation for us … and that’s what resulted in litigation, because to his mind, only his complaints were not heard and addressed by the condo association,” Braithwaite said.

According to Braithwaite, Lambert had been in “great spirits” in the days leading up to the shooting, giving no indication that anything was wrong.

White House Shooting Suspect Dead After Exchanging Gunfire With Police

What Happened Inside the VIDA Gym?

D.C.’s Metropolitan Police Department first alerted the public on social media that there was an active shooter in the area of 15th Street and P Street in Logan Circle on Thursday morning. During the press conference, Carroll said the shooting began inside VIDA, where one person was killed. Roughly 50 gym members evacuated after hearing loud bangs.

As officers moved through the scene, they cleared the gym and the apartment building on the same block. Authorities then heard gunshots coming from the seventh floor of the apartment building and determined the gunman had barricaded himself inside a unit.

Negotiators made contact with him and spoke with him for more than an hour before hearing a single gunshot. Officers forced their way into the apartment and found him dead.

Witnesses Recount the Gym Shooting

The attack left Logan Circle residents reeling, and one witness described the confusion of those first moments to WJLA.

“I hear a loud bang. So at first, everyone’s confused. I’m confused. Everyone else is confused. And I go towards the commotion area. And I see someone lying on the floor,” Anthony Mirones, who was inside the gym at the time, said.

Mirones recalled that another man with “a better view” of the shooting “looks back behind me and tells me, like, ‘He’s dead.’ So I’m like, ‘What?’”

“I get a little closer. I see he’s on the floor; I see some blood,” Mirones said. “So I think, OK, I’m connecting to all this loud bang. I think, ‘gunshot.’”

Actor Zachary Levi Details ‘Commotion’ Inside Ballroom During WHCD Shooting

A fire alarm was pulled to get people out of the building. “Everyone evacuated eventually pretty quickly and then we’re outside the entrance of the Vida Fitness, and police officers start coming to run inside and then another police officer is outside the entrance asking ‘What’s the description of this guy?’” Mirones said.

Who Was Matt Lambert?

Before the shooting, Lambert had built a career in emergency medicine and had more recently pivoted to work as a healthcare consultant. Public records and his attorney’s account paint a picture of a man with multiple properties and significant resources who had grown fixated on a single legal fight over his D.C. home.

That fight will now outlive him only as a matter of civil record. For the families of the people he shot—especially Stuart’s loved ones—the question of why a long-running dispute over mold and maintenance ended in gunfire inside a neighborhood gym is one the courts can no longer answer.

title: Phil Collins Considers Touring Again After Years of Health Problems
content:
Phil Collins has not given up on the possibility of touring again despite spending the better part of 20 years battling numerous health problems.

“Never say never … I do think, every now and again, that I’m not finished [touring],” Collins, 75, revealed in a recent interview with the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. “On the other hand, I think of the practicalities.”

Those everyday “practicalities” would include giving up his current lifestyle for the grueling physical toll of life on the road.

“I’ll enjoy the sunshine, you know, just there’s no sweat, don’t have to do anything. Just get up and say, ‘What am I going to do today?'” he said. “But on the other hand, once you’ve been on stage all your life and tasted that, it’s difficult to stop.”

Phil Collins Hospitalized for Surgery: Report

As for the possibility of releasing new music, Collins teased, “I’ve got ideas. I got things I finished. I’ve got things that I’ve half finished.”

Collins has struggled with various health issues, including type 2 diabetes, for many years. In February 2025, he told Mojo that he was no longer “hungry” to keep playing music because he’d been “very sick.”

The rocker suffered a serious spinal injury in 2007 that caused nerve damage. While the injury initially left him completely incapable of playing drums, he underwent corrective surgery in 2015.

Collins recovered well enough to reunite with Genesis bandmates Tony Banks and Mike Rutherford for the group’s The Last Domino? Tour in 2021, though his physical limitations mandated that Collins perform from a chair.

The “In the Air Tonight” musician told BBC Radio 2’s Zoe Ball in January that he now had “a 24-hour live-in nurse” as a result of undergoing five knee surgeries.

“I’ve had challenges with my knee… I had everything that could go wrong with me, did go wrong with me,” he explained.

Collins’ health problems got so serious in 2024 that his five children — daughters Lily and Joely and sons Simon, Nicolas and Matthew — were summoned to his bedside to say their goodbyes.

Phil Collins Reveals 14-Year Feud With Paul McCartney: 'You F--k’

“Because there were some decisions to be made about ‘Do we keep Phil on life support?’” he shared with The Sunday Times in August. “My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up. People were coming to say goodbye.”

He continued, “But I don’t remember them coming. I didn’t have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn’t see me again. It could all have gone so terribly wrong.”

Collins made a major life change in 2024 when he stopped drinking alcohol after experiencing serious complications with his kidneys.

“I guess I had too much of it,” he told BBC Radio 2 in January. “I was never drunk, although I fell over a couple of times. But it is just one of those things that happened and it all caught up with me, and I spent months in hospital.”

An encouraging milestone for Collins will take place on Saturday, November 14, when he is inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo act alongside Oasis, the Wu-Tang Clan, Celia Cruz and producer Rick Rubin at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater. (The band Genesis was previously inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2010.)

title: How Did Investigators Find Baby Who Survived Being Buried Alive? What to Know
content:
The astonishing rescue of an 11-month-old baby who spent roughly 24 hours underground inside a dog crate has gripped a community in South Carolina and drawn national attention to a case authorities are calling miraculous. 

Koah Sharp was pulled from the dirt alive on November 10, 2026, after his father allegedly took him from a relative’s care and buried him in the woods near Batesburg-Leesville.

Us breaks down what is known about how investigators located the boy, the charges against his father and the small details that may have saved Koah’s life.

How Investigators Found Koah Sharp

A search party combing the area around the home of the suspect’s father noticed a patch of “freshly disturbed” dirt on the afternoon of November 10, 2026, according to Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon.

Investigators began digging and soon heard the baby crying from beneath the soil, a sound Koon described at a news conference as “the most joyful sound.” 

Koah was found inside what Koon called a dog crate wrapped in a towel, and authorities believe that towel, combined with colder temperatures, likely created an air pocket that allowed him to survive.

“So as you imagine, the race was on. Everybody’s getting down there trying to get him out,” Koon said. 

The sheriff said Koah was “screaming at the top of his lungs” when rescuers reached him. 

He was rushed to a hospital and released that same evening, according to the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department, which announced in a November 11 news release that “Koah Sharp is alive and well.”

Who Is Michael Comer, the Father Charged in the Case

Michael Comer, Koah’s father, was arrested and now faces charges of attempted murder, unlawful conduct toward a child, custodial interference and burglary, according to the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department. 

He was initially taken into custody on a burglary charge on the evening of November 9, 2026, after being located at an outbuilding in Batesburg without the baby. He was denied bond on November 12.

Tyler Douglas, the lead investigator with the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department, told a judge that Comer showed no remorse for the attempted murder of his son, according to reporting from the Associated Press and CBS News. 

Last month, Comer pleaded guilty to a domestic violence charge and was sentenced to probation, per the Associated Press. He has reportedly not yet been appointed legal counsel.

What Happened Before Koah Sharp Disappeared Near Batesburg-Leesville

Koah was in the care of his paternal grandmother on November 9, 2026, when Comer arrived at her home. 

“She left Koah with Comer to run an errand while another caregiver was coming over,” Koon said in a statement. “When the caregiver got there, Comer was gone and Koah was with him.” 

A desperate search was launched across the area around Batesburg-Leesville, with the sheriff’s office posting on Facebook a description of a blue-eyed “bright boy” with reddish blond hair who regularly uses a pacifier.

Patricia Comer, Michael’s mother and Koah’s grandmother, told NBC News that her son is “where he needs to be” following his arrest. “Honestly, I’m his mother, and I never expected this from him,” she told the outlet.

Baby’s Grandfather Describes the Rescue

John Comer, the suspect’s father and Koah’s grandfather, told the Associated Press that he witnessed his grandson being pulled from the ground on the property near his home. He said the baby was crying and covered in dirt when rescuers lifted him out.

“I became ecstatic, my hands straight in the air. I’m looking in the sky, jumping up and down, praising God,” John said. “And at the same time I hit my knees and I’m just crying.”

What’s Next for Koah Sharp and the Criminal Case

Koah was released from the hospital the evening of his rescue, and Koon said he “hopefully will make a full recovery.” The sheriff’s office initially spelled the boy’s last name as Sharpe before updating it to Sharp in subsequent releases. Comer remains in custody after being denied bond, and information about his legal representation was not immediately available at the time of the sheriff’s department’s announcements.

Investigators have continued to emphasize the narrow margin by which the baby was found alive, pointing to the towel-wrapped crate and the cooler weather as the likely reasons an air pocket formed beneath the dirt.

title: Search Continues for Confidential Informant Who Vanished Over 10 Years Ago
content:
A Pennsylvania woman’s disappearance remains unsolved more than 10 years after she vanished before she was set to testify as a confidential informant.

Investigators continue to search for Danielle M. Drozdowski, a Wilkes-Barre resident who went missing in 2014 at the age of 25, according to a Tuesday, November 10, news release from Pennsylvania State Police’s organization, PSP Tips.

Drozdowski “was a confidential informant who was scheduled to testify before a grand jury in August of 2014, however she failed to appear and was subsequently entered as ‘wanted,’” state police said.

Authorities are offering a $5,000 reward for information solving her disappearance. She would be 37 years old today.

Search Intensifies for Maine Teen Stefanie Damron 2 Years After She Vanished

Family and friends haven’t seen or heard from Drozdowski since March 19, 2014, the last time she shared a post to Facebook, according to police.

“Her last known location and what she was last wearing are unknown,” police said.

Drozdowski is white, has blue eyes and is described as around 5-foot-2 or 5-foot-3, and weighing around 120 to 165 pounds by the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs).

She also has several tattoos, including on both of her hands, her left arm and the back of her neck.

She has the outline of an “Om” symbol tattooed on her neck, according to NamUS. On her right hand, she has a tattoo of a possible shamrock. On her left arm, she has a multi-color skull tattoo and flowers.

She also has a tattoo of an anchor on her left hand.

Man Led Detectives to Missing Woman's Remains 7 Years After He Killed Her

A woman who commented under PSP Tips’ Facebook news release wrote Drozdowski was her former best friend.

“She was my best friend at one point in time in school, played on the basketball team together did everything together she didn’t have an easy life growing up but she was trying too make the best of it,” the woman, Samantha Lynn, wrote in the comment left under the post.

“I hope and pray she is out there some where and is okay her friends & family miss her terribly,” the comment also said.

Anyone with information on Drozdowski is asked to call Pennsylvania State Police’s Wilkes-Barre station at 570-821-4110 or PSP Tips Toll Free at 1-800-472-8477. Tips can also be shared online.

The news release stated, “All callers to PSP Tips could be eligible for a CASH REWARD for information that leads to an arrest, the solving of a crime/cold case or the location of a wanted person/fugitive or missing person.”

title: Siblings Derek and Julianne Hough's Candid Quotes About Dancing Together
content:
Derek Hough and Julianne Hough have spent nearly two decades sharing the Dancing With the Stars ballroom — and along the way, their on-screen chemistry has sparked more than a few raised eyebrows from fans who forgot (or never knew) the pros are brother and sister.

The siblings joined DWTS in 2007, eventually racking up a combined eight mirrorball trophies. Derek now judges alongside Carrie Ann Inaba and Bruno Tonioli, while Julianne cohosts the show with Alfonso Ribeiro. Over the years, they’ve opened up about the perks — and the awkward moments — of dancing together in front of millions.

Here’s everything the Hough siblings have said about performing together:

‘DWTS’ at 20: Derek and Julianne Hough Get Tearful About Why It's 'Home'

Julianne Hough Recalls Why Fans Were Convinced They Were a Couple

Julianne and her brother’s first joint DWTS performance left audiences very confused.

Appearing on a September 2025 episode of the “Chicks in the Office” podcast, Julianne recalled Inaba choreographing a rumba — commonly known as “the dance of love” — for the siblings to perform on the live tour.

“Our first thing that we ever did on Dancing With the Stars was we were both on the live tour,” she said at the time. “Carrie Ann was the one [who] choreographed everything, and she got us to do a rumba together.”

The billing didn’t help clear things up.

“Our names in the program were ‘Derek and Julianne Hough,’ so everybody thought we were married and we were doing this rumba,” Julianne noted. “When people found out we were brother-sister, I remember there was one venue … and we just heard, ‘That’s just wrong!'”

Robin Wright Thought Derek and Julianne Hough Were Married

The confusion extends well beyond live-tour audiences.

At the 2026 Golden Globe Awards, Damsel actress Robin Wright admitted to Extra host Derek that she’d assumed he and Julianne were a couple.

“Wait, you’re the brother of Julianne, I love her,” Wright told Derek at the time. “You guys are amazing together. I follow you guys on Instagram and watch you guys move. … Can I tell you something? When I first saw her dance, I was like, ‘They’re married.'”

Derek took it in stride, replying, “I’ve got that sometimes.”

Derek Hough’s Awkward ‘Tell Me About It’ Moment

Derek Hough nodded to the sibling-dance awkwardness during a November 2026 live episode of DWTS. When Paralympian Ezra Frech and pro partner Daniella Karagach performed an intimate Grammy Night Argentine tango after admitting in rehearsals that they felt like siblings, Inaba joked that Frech had turned his “sister into [his] lover” for the number.

“Sister to lover that’s awkward,” Ribeiro chimed in.

“Tell me about it, that was weird,” Derek added.

Fans quickly speculated the comment referenced his dynamic with Julianne. “Derek adding in ‘tell me about it’ after Carrie Ann gave Ezra and Daniella credit for doing an intimate dance when they said they feel like siblings HAD ME GIGGGGGGLING,” one fan wrote via Threads.

Julianne reposted the Threads comment to her Instagram Stories, adding a shrugging-woman emoji.

Julianne and Derek Hough’s Sibling Bond Powers Their Performing Partnership

Speaking to Us in November 2025, the siblings gushed about one another.

“I’m Derek’s biggest fan,” Julianne exclusively shared with Us. “He’s always the first person to recognize and see me for who I am. He always has my back, and I know I can trust that my brother is always there because he’s shown up that way.”

Derek returned the praise, telling Us, “I actually want to give Jules her flowers. When she came on the show, she changed the trajectory of DWTS forever. She became the model of what we see now — that multifaceted dancer. She came in and disrupted the whole scene.”
